text: Homeowners hate paying before the leak is fixed.
Plumbers hate waiting 45 days to get paid.
VeriPay:
PayPal holds the money without charging it, AI checks the work, and the pro is paid the moment it passes.
Maria asks in her own words.
Our model writes the definition of done, with a typical price range.
Pros' agents bid.
Hers counters and hires at $185, inside a signed mandate capped at $200.
A lower cap, or a replay, is refused.
PayPal authorizes $200:
held, not charged.
On site, a $47.05 valve is over her agent's limit, so only Maria's PIN can approve it, and PayPal re-holds $247.05 on her saved card.
The plumber sends photos and the receipt from his phone.
Our models read the photos and the receipt;
code checks when and where each was taken.
A note hiding an instruction is flagged, and the money waits for a person.
Every check passed:
code captures exactly $232.05, one Payouts batch pays the pro, and an agent reconciles both with PayPal.
Any agent can drive it, over MCP, A2A or REST.
But every money move passes one guard in our code:
limits, PIN, signed mandates.
The money itself runs on PayPal.
We fine-tuned 0.6-billion-parameter models from a 30-billion open teacher.
Code writes every label;
the teacher only the wording.
On held-out tests, the audit model gets 99.9% of verdicts right, its teacher 68, and it runs on a CPU in about three seconds.
Under the hood it's all PayPal:
Orders authorizes, the Vault re-holds, a partial capture takes what's due, Payouts pays the pro, and the Agent Toolkit reconciles.
It scales to materials, Pay Later, landlords and neighbors, with an AG Grid back office.
Forty-five AI agents tested it for eleven rounds;
every blocker was fixed.
VeriPay.
The money waits for the proof.
